# iliad-061 — new renderings (10.295–389)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς ἔφαν εὐχόμενοι, τῶν δ’ ἔκλυε Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη (10.295, whole line, plural) | "So they spoke, praying, and Pallas Athena heard them." | "So they prayed, and Pallas Athena heard them." | "them heard Pallas Athena"; follows the shipped singular (iliad-028, odyssey-012) with the pronoun changed |
| Τρῶες ἀγήνορες (10.299) | "the manly Trojans" | "the proud Trojans" | "lordly" (the Odyssey's μνηστῆρες ἀγήνορες "lordly suitors"; a departure, because the Iliad's own row fixes ἀγήνωρ as "manly" / "proud", θυμὸς ἀγήνωρ "manly spirit" / "proud spirit"), "arrogant" |
| οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδέ (10.299) | "Nor again … either" | "… would not … either" | "not even" (the second οὐδέ is "either", not "even") |
| μισθὸς ἄρκιος (10.304) | "the wage … sufficient" | "the pay … ample" (+ note: ἄρκιος "sufficient", "assured" also given) | "sure", "firm", "fixed"; ἄρκιος from ἀρκέω "suffice" |
| ἐριαύχενες ἵπποι (10.305) | "strong-necked horses" | "strong-necked horses" (+ note: exact sense of ἐρι- not known) | "thick-necked", "high-necked", "arch-necked", "proud-necked" (each decides the unknown) |
| πολύχαλκος (10.315) | "rich in bronze" | "rich in bronze" | "bronze-rich", "wealthy in bronze"; built like πολύχρυσος "rich in gold" (7.180 and the Odyssey) |
| κήρυξ θεῖος (κήρυκος θείοιο, 10.315) | "a divine herald" | "the divine herald" | "godlike", "noble"; follows the table's Ταλθύβιον θεῖον κήρυκα |
| εἶδος μὲν ἔην κακός (10.316) | "in form was bad" | "was ugly to look at" | "of poor build", "unlovely"; κακός "bad" in `l`, the sense (looks) in `i` |
| ἀνάσχεο (σκῆπτρον ἀνάσχεο, 10.321) | "hold up" | "hold up" | "endure", "hold out" (the sense of τέτλαθι … ἀνάσχεο, iliad-006 and iliad-030; here the object is the sceptre, so the verb is physical) |
| ἅλιος σκοπός · ἀπὸ δόξης (10.324) | "a lookout in vain" · "away from expectation" | "a lookout in vain" · "fall short of what you expect" (+ note: the exact sense of ἀπὸ δόξης not certain) | "idle lookout" (ἅλιος "in vain" at 4.498 is not "idle"), "without aim", "off the mark" |
| ἀγλαϊεῖσθαι (10.331, future infinitive) | "take splendour in" | "take proud delight in" (+ note: exact nuance not known) | "glory in" (κῦδος is "glory"), "revel", "show off"; ἀγλαΐη "splendour" (odyssey table) |
| διαμπερές (of time, 10.331) | "right through" | "continually" / "go on …" | "for ever" (adds a claim), "to the end"; `l` keeps the table's "right through" (7.171) |
| ἐπίορκον ἐπώμοσε (10.332) | "swore a false oath" | "swore a false oath" | "perjured himself", "swore falsely"; follows ἐπίορκον ὀμόσσῃ (3.279) |
| ὀροθύνω (τὸν δ’ ὀρόθυνεν, 10.332) | "roused" | "roused" | "stirred up", "incited" (reserved for ἀνίημι "urge on"), "urged on" (ὀτρύνω) |
| κτιδέη κυνέη (10.335) | "a weasel-skin helmet" | "a weasel-skin helmet" (+ note: κτίς weasel, marten or polecat, not known) | "marten-skin cap" (decides the animal), "cat-skin", "fur cap"; κυνέη "helmet" as in the table |
| ἕσσατο ῥινὸν πολιοῖο λύκοιο (10.334) | "clothed himself … in the skin of a grey wolf" | "clothed himself … in the skin of a grey wolf" | "wolfskin cloak", "hide of a hoary wolf"; ῥινός "skin" (5.308), πολιός "grey" |
| οὐδ’ ἄρ’ ἔμελλεν … ἀποίσειν (10.336) | "nor was he then destined … to carry back" | "he was never to … carry word" | "was not going to", "was fated"; follows the Odyssey's οὐδ’ ἄρ’ ἔμελλεν … "not then destined" |
| διογενὴς Ὀδυσσεύς (10.340) | "Zeus-sprung Odysseus" | "Zeus-born Odysseus" | "god-born", "heaven-born"; follows the table's διογενής |
| τὸν δὲ φράσατο προσιόντα (10.339) | "and him noticed approaching" | "noticed him coming" | "saw", "marked"; φράζομαι "notice" |
| ἀλλ’ ἐῶμεν … παρεξελθεῖν (10.344) | "let us allow him … to pass by" | "let us … let him go past us" | "let him go on", "let him through" |
| προτιειλεῖν (10.347) | "press" | "keep pressing" (+ note: rare verb, "drive, hem in") | "herd", "chase", "drive" |
| ὁδοῦ παρέξ (10.349) | "aside from the road" | "stepping aside from the road" | "off the road", "out of the way" |
| ὃ δ’ ἄρ’ ὦκα παρέδραμεν ἀφραδίῃσιν (10.350) | "he quickly ran past, in follies" | "ran quickly past in his folly" | "heedlessly", "carelessly"; ἀφραδίῃσιν "follies" / "folly" (table) |
| οὖρα ἡμιόνων (10.351) | "furrow-lengths of mules" | "the length of a mule-team's furrow" (+ note: exact length not known) | "a mule's cast", "a mule's range", "the distance of a plough-team's turn" |
| νειὸς βαθείη (10.353) | "deep fallow land" | "deep fallow land" | "deep soil", "deep field"; νειός "fallow" |
| δοῦπον ἀκούσας (10.354) | "a crash having heard" | "heard the crash" | "thud", "roar" (avoided by the table), "noise", "tramp" |
| ἀποστρέψοντας (10.355) | "to turn him back" | "to turn him back" | "to call him back", "to bring him back"; future participle of purpose |
| Ἕκτορος ὀτρύναντος (10.356) | "Hector having urged them on" | "since Hector had urged them on" | "at Hector's command" (ὀτρύνω is "urge") |
| δουρηνεκές (10.357) | "a spear-cast" | "a spear's cast" | "a spear-throw", "as far as a spear flies"; formation δόρυ + ἐνεγκεῖν |
| γνῶ ῥ’ ἄνδρας δηΐους (10.358) | "knew them for hostile men" | "knew them for enemies" | "recognised the enemy"; δήϊος "hostile" as in the table |
| λαιψηρά (γούνατ’ ἐνώμα, 10.358) | "quick" | "quick" | "nimble" (ῥίμφα "nimbly" is reserved), "swift" (reserved for θοός / ὠκύς), "light", "supple" |
| γούνατ’ ἐνώμα φευγέμεναι (10.358) | "his … knees he set moving to flee" | "set his … knees moving in flight" | "ran", "took to his heels"; νωμάω "ply" (table 5.594: "wield") |
| τοὶ δ’ αἶψα διώκειν ὁρμήθησαν (10.359) | "and they at once rushed to pursue" | "and the two at once rushed to pursue him" | "set out in pursuit", "launched"; ὁρμάω "rush" |
| καρχαρόδοντε κύνε (10.360) | "two sharp-toothed dogs" | "two sharp-toothed hounds" | "jagged-toothed", "sharp-fanged", "white-toothed" (ἀργιόδους is "white-toothed" in the Odyssey table); dual kept |
| κεμάς (10.361) | "a young deer" | "a young deer" (+ note: some take "hornless deer"; not certain) | "fawn", "doe", "hind" |
| λαγωός (10.361) | "hare" | "hare" | "rabbit" |
| ἐπείγετον (10.361) | "press hard" | "press … hard" | "chase", "harry" |
| ἐμμενὲς αἰεί (10.361, 10.364) | "steadily, always" | "steadily, without pause" / "unceasingly" | "relentlessly", "doggedly", "ceaselessly" |
| χῶρον ἀν’ ὑλήενθ’ (10.362) | "through a wooded place" | "through wooded country" | "wooded ground", "forested land"; ὑλήεις "wooded" (table) |
| ὃ δέ τε προθέῃσι μεμηκώς (10.362) | "and it runs on ahead, bleating" | "while it runs on ahead, bleating" | "crying out", "panting", "baying"; μηκάομαι "bleat" (table, μηκάδες αἶγες) |
| ἀποτμήξαντε (λαοῦ, 10.364) | "having cut him off from the people" | "cut him off from the army" | "severed", "intercepted", "headed off"; ἀποτμήγω "cut off" |
| μένος ἔμβαλ’ Ἀθήνη (10.366) | "Athena cast might into" | "Athena put might into" | "strength" (reserved for κράτος and σθένος), "courage"; μένος "might" (table 2.387) |
| ἐπευξάμενος βαλέειν (10.368) | "to vaunt that he had struck" | "to cry out in triumph that he had struck the man" | "to pray", "to boast" alone (ἐπεύχεται 5.119 is "vaunts" / "cries out in triumph"); ἐπεύχομαι "pray" belongs to the prayer-sense (3.350) |
| φθαίη … ὃ δὲ δεύτερος ἔλθοι (10.368) | "might be first … and he come second" | "could be first … leaving Diomedes to come second" | "beat him to it" in `l`, "come after" |
| ἠὲ μέν’ ἠέ σε δουρὶ κιχήσομαι (10.370) | "Either stand, or with my spear I shall reach you" | "Either stand still, or I shall reach you with my spear" | "halt", "stop", "wait"; κιχάνω "overtake", "catch" (also κιχήτην "came up with"); κιχάνω is "reach" |
| ἑκὼν δ’ ἡμάρτανε φωτός (10.372) | "willingly he missed the man" | "missed the man on purpose" | "deliberately" in `l`, "intentionally"; ἑκών "willingly" (table, 4.43 ἑκών) |
| ἐΰξου δουρός (10.373) | "well-polished spear" | "well-polished spear" | "well-planed", "smooth"; follows the table's ἐΰξοον |
| τάρβησε … βαμβαίνων (10.374) | "was terrified, stammering" | "terrified and stammering" (+ note: βαμβαίνων not certain) | "trembling", "chattering" (kept for ἄραβος) |
| ἄραβος ὀδόντων (10.375) | "a clatter … of his teeth" | "his teeth began to clatter" (+ note: ἄραβος derivation not known) | "chattering", "rattle", "gnashing"; the root is sound-imitating |
| χλωρὸς ὑπαὶ δείους (10.376) | "pale beneath fear" | "pale with fear" | "green with fear", "yellow with terror"; χλωρός "pale" (table, χλωρὸν δέος) |
| τὼ δ’ ἀσθμαίνοντε κιχήτην (10.376) | "the two, panting, came up with him" | "the two came up with him, panting" | "gasping", "breathless" |
| χειρῶν ἁψάσθην (10.377) | "took hold of his hands" | "took hold of his hands" | "seized", "grasped", "clasped"; ἅπτομαι "take hold of" |
| ἔπος ηὔδα, δακρύσας (10.377) | "in tears, spoke a word" | "said, in tears" | "weeping", "wept and said"; follows 4.348 δακρύσας "in tears" |
| ζωγρεῖτ’ (10.378) | "Take me alive" | "Take me alive" | "Capture me", "spare me", "make me prisoner"; follows ζώγρει (6.46) |
| αὐτὰρ ἐγὼν ἐμὲ λύσομαι (10.378) | "and I shall ransom myself" | "and I will ransom myself" | "buy my freedom", "pay for my release"; λύω "ransom" (λυσόμενος 1.13) |
| ἔστι γὰρ ἔνδον (10.378) | "for there is within" | "for inside there are" | "in my house", "at home"; the house is the father's but the Greek has only ἔνδον |
| καταθύμιος (10.383) | "in-your-heart" | "on your mind" | "pleasing", "desired", "dear"; built on κατά + θυμός as in τό μοι καταθύμιόν ἐστιν (Odyssey 22.392) |
| πῇ δὴ οὕτως … ἔρχεαι (10.385) | "Whither, then, thus … do you go" | "Where are you going like this" | "How do you come", "Why do you go"; πῇ "whither" (direction) |
| προέηκε διασκοπιᾶσθαι ἕκαστα (10.388) | "send you forth to spy out each thing" | "send you out to spy out everything" | "scout", "examine", "reconnoitre"; ἕκαστα "each thing" |
| ἦ σ’ αὐτὸν θυμὸς ἀνῆκε (10.389) | "Or did your own heart urge you on?" | "Or did your own heart urge you on?" | "impel", "send you", "set you loose"; ἀνίημι "urge on" (5.405 ἀνῆκε "has urged on") |

Departures from the Odyssey's wording (all listed above): Τρῶες ἀγήνορες "manly / proud Trojans" (Odyssey's "lordly suitors" for μνηστῆρες ἀγήνορες, because the Iliad's own ἀγήνωρ row fixes "manly" / "proud"); λαιψηρά "quick" (no row in either table; "nimble" is the Odyssey's rendering of ῥίμφα and is kept for it).

Lines reused word for word (no new rendering): 10.302 (= 2.55), 10.313 (= 3.95, English ends in ";" as shipped), 10.382 (Odyssey), 10.384 (Odyssey 1.169); 10.327 second line (= 10.147), 10.379 and 10.381 (= 6.48, 6.50), 10.386 (= 10.83), the first line of 10.319 (= 10.220).
